title: Personal development readiness blocked by inherited eager squash merge caller
body:
The personal-fork development route is blocked from safe readiness by Knoxx's inherited eager merge caller. At fork main `b3903dfc4c9e9dd5e32ae658cf5d8abb88b8e792` and accepted origin main `3409977bca4ba35e09967f9a99d50867a679a73c`, `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml` runs for a ready same-repository PR and invokes pinned eta-mu workflow `0823119585244bc5dfeea3c2b4cd64b0b0aa7cef` with `merge-method:SQUASH`. The caller contains no canonical current-head review/required-check/convergence admission.

The user requires development PRs on personal forks, auto-merge off until qualification, merge commits, and separately qualified release/deploy PRs into origin. Synchronization https://github.com/riatzukiza/knoxx/pull/1 is therefore draft/autooff; the separate replacement of origin381 will also stay draft. Fork metadata currently reports `allow_auto_merge:false` and squash enabled, but settings are not reviewed enforcement. Personal issues are disabled, so the gap is recorded in the owning origin repository without changing settings.

Scope: separately review and repair the inherited readiness trigger/base enforcement so ready cannot start eager merge before canonical qualification and explicit merge authority. Preserve exact source/head/base binding, native reviewers, required checks and review convergence. Do not fix this by enabling squash, widening permissions, removing checks, transferring old approvals, or merging a feature merely for validation.

No merge attempt, deployment, secret/config/protection/settings change, or cross-lane interference occurred in this preparation. This is a concrete readiness blocker discovered by inspecting the actual callable workflow. Related owning-repository instance: open-hax/proxx#454.

title: Restore a callable and head-bound Kimi review invitation

labels.name: blocked
labels.description: Concrete PR qualification or external blocker; see evidence comment

body:
Knoxx's current `.github/workflows/opencode-code-review.yml` exposes only `workflow_dispatch`, but its review job requires `github.event.pull_request.draft == false` and `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`. A dispatch event has no pull-request payload, so the documented Kimi invitation surface cannot execute the review job. This is a concrete workflow contract gap, separate from missing approval or paid review quota.

Observed against PR #381 head `40221a69f7fff675b46614d9ab318b4ef52f3786`: the workflow has no dispatch inputs for a PR number/head, and its concurrency expression also uses an absent pull-request number. Its provider invocation still names the legacy `kimi-for-coding/k2p5` model, whose availability must be verified before restoring invitations. No dispatch was attempted merely to produce a predictable skip.

Acceptance:

- Expose an authorized, bounded invitation surface that resolves an actual PR and verifies its immutable current head before reading candidate code.
- Preserve a trusted pinned workflow and least-privilege read-only candidate execution; do not solve this by enabling privileged candidate-selected code.
- Verify the provider/model and its authenticated native GitHub identity. Missing availability or identity remains visible, and no review quota response, skip, or generic bot output is treated as an approval.
- Deduplicate requests per PR/head, isolate concurrent review workers, and produce complete head-bound findings/verdict evidence consumed by the canonical PR flow.
- Keep auto-merge off until the separate exact-head qualification contract passes.

Relevant existing work: [Proxx review transport repair PR #445](https://github.com/open-hax/proxx/pull/445), as a reference for its actual verified mechanisms rather than an instruction to copy unrelated repository policy. This gap currently contributes to the unavailable reviewer surfaces recorded on [Knoxx PR #381](https://github.com/open-hax/knoxx/pull/381).

title: Delegate local Knoxx login to Axxium

labels.name: blocked

body:
When `KNOXX_AXXIUM_ORIGIN` points at local Axxium, Knoxx now accepts loopback HTTP for development, labels the delegated password form clearly, and treats an anonymous auth-context response as an ordinary signed-out visit. HTTPS remains required for non-loopback authorities. The local PM2 verifier checks rejected anonymous and wrong-password requests, delegated login, signup closure, actor context, and logout; the browser tour captures the login UI.

Validation: the live local delegation verifier passed; frontend typecheck and 456 CLJS tests (2,046 assertions) passed with zero compiler warnings; backend typecheck and the JS boundary check passed. The modified backend extern lints with zero warnings. The repository-wide backend lint remains red on pre-existing file-size errors and warnings in unrelated files.


Migration infrastructure: yes

This PR wires Knoxx to the existing Axxium identity authority and adds local verification infrastructure. It changes the existing Helix login surface but introduces no new legacy TypeScript source, bridge export, or route. No TypeScript migration slice is claimed.

title: [305] Bound authorized run-directory pagination before HTTP adoption
[305/03b] Mongo policy modules and legacy authentication compatibility
body:
The Mongo policy facade mixes directory, role, credential and invitation operations in one large module. This PR extracts named modules and fixes mutations while preserving the preceding authentication runtime, so the provider changes can be reviewed before verified-identity activation.

Tracks #374; part of #323 / #305. Depends on additive foundation #375. Identity runtime activation remains #335. This draft will follow the prior PRs through current-main integration, both reviewers and an exact-head merge.

Behavior changes:
- Omitted admin roles preserve current grants; an explicit empty set removes them. Scoped profile changes preserve other tenants. Unsupported Mongo profile/status updates return400 instead of pretending success.
- Assigned actor coordinates cannot be reassigned. Native CAS admits one initial owner; conflicting writes refuse before changing role/profile/projection state.
- Invitation claims reserve before provisioning, use owned CAS transitions and release only a known failed reservation. Concurrent and uncertain claims cannot provision twice. Legacy HTTP preserves classified403/409/503 failures.
- Repeated remote identity context keeps existing membership, roles and profile; narrow HTTP status/code helpers preserve the new errors. Production bootstrap, auth/session/authz, configuration and frontend keep the preceding behavior.

Qualification at the same final backend tree `f15b5370`: **1,811 backend tests / 8,389 assertions**, **72 Node checks**, server compilation562files/zero warnings, and **78 tests / 372 assertions** in the native human proof. This includes real owned Mongo replica/TLS/Fastify remote and local login, repeated context, admin PATCH, invitation CAS, restart/key recovery and logout. The prior admin/invite caller bodies reproduce9failures; old shared status helpers reproduce2failures. Final portable proof at `33724ee7` passes66tests/283assertions. Node22 preflight refuses before fixture work.

Run `scripts/verify-policy-provider-foundation.sh`, or set `KNOXX_TEST_MONGOD` to a local qualified Mongo executable and add `--native`. The script requires Node>=24 on PATH, Clojure, OpenSSL and installed pinned dependencies. See `docs/verification/policy-module-recovery.md`; `policy-provider-boundary.json` records exact moved/restored paths for later activation.

Limits: this retains the preceding authentication admission semantics; it does not activate the verified-principal runtime or invitation UI. Native restart means the owned Mongo process plus a new Fastify application and persisted session key, not a whole PM2/Node service restart. Uncertain invitation completion requires explicit recovery; no cross-store rollback or claim-stealing guarantee is made. Five inherited lint warnings remain in unchanged functions/file sizes; owned scan has zero errors and no new/touched-function warnings. No live application service/database is used, and no full strict-lint pass is claimed.

title: Reconcile PR #305 identity, deployment and CMS changes with current main
body:
Parent: #323. Blocks merging every split of #305.

# PR #305 main reconciliation candidate

Status: intentionally incomplete; no merge commit or tree produced, no push.

- Worktree: `/tmp/knoxx-pr305-split/reconcile`
- Branch: `codex/pr305-reconcile-main`
- Parent/main: `c33b7623` (origin/main)
- Incoming PR snapshot: `1d3b207a` (origin/pr305)
- Remaining conflict: `backend/src/cljs/knoxx/backend/infra/routes/auth.cljs`
- Main workspace and original PR branches were not changed.

## Integration blocker: incompatible identity ownership

Current main uses the configured remote HTTPS Axxium service through
`infra.auth.axxium`: password verification goes to that host, Knoxx retains
its own session and local membership, and existing login/signup/config/invite
routes retain their Knoxx implementations. This is documented by main's
`docs/verification/environment-and-cross-host-acceptance.md` and exercised by
its cross-host workflow script.

PR #305 replaces `infra.routes.auth` with the embedded Axxium plugin and
mandatory initialized identity context. `extern.axxium/options` selects
`:provider :edn`; `infra.identity` authenticates against its local service,
requires stable principal bindings, and rejects the old asserted identity
headers. Its documented browser cookie is `axxium_session`. Signup, credential
management, and OAuth ownership move to Axxium. This is documented in
`docs/architecture/axxium-policy-adoption.md`.

Neither taking main nor taking #305 for auth.cljs preserves both behaviors.
Preserving main's file alone is insufficient because #305 also changes
identity bootstrap, policy, session, authorization, and MCP paths; retaining
#305's file alone silently disconnects main's configured remote identity
provider and its working cross-host acceptance flow. No identity migration or
provider-composition design is inferred for a PR-splitting task.

Required task before merge: reconcile the remote-provider deployment contract
with embedded Axxium adoption; explicitly decide supported providers, preserve
or deliberately migrate immutable bindings and sessions, keep signup/config/
invite/credential routes coherent, test cross-host sign-in and anonymous
refusal, update the two architecture/verification documents, and rerun the
relevant identity/MCP suites. Source #305 should remain an immutable reference.

## Mechanical candidate decisions

| Path | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| `.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml` | Keep main's rewritten SHA qualification/integration/e2e/mutation workflow. PR's only new intent here was installing clj-kondo; transport that to the shared setup action. |
| `.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml` | Preserve main's deletion; do not resurrect the retired staging workflow just to install clj-kondo. |
| `.github/actions/knoxx-setup/action.yml` | Add `clj-kondo: latest` to the existing setup-clojure step shared by current qualification workflows. |
| `backend/deps.edn` | Retain main's pinned document-history library and add PR's pinned Clio/Axxium libraries. Preserve each existing SHA. |
| `backend/package.json` | Union main's fs-ext-extra-prebuilt and build allowlist with PR identity dependencies including jose. |
| `backend/pnpm-lock.yaml` | Union the single jose importer conflict; both sides' package and snapshot entries were already auto-merged. |
| `backend/shadow-cljs.edn` | Retain main's CMS history targets and PR's recovery/identity/wiki verification targets. |
| `backend/src/cljs/knoxx/backend/infra/routes/app.cljs` | Preserve PR's extracted route composition. Main's only semantic addition here is CMS document route registration; move it into the extracted publication registrar. |
| `backend/src/cljs/knoxx/backend/infra/routes/app/publication.cljs` | Register main's CMS document adapter immediately after CMS publication routes, with the same runtime/helpers arguments. |
| `backend/src/cljs/knoxx/backend/infra/routes/cms_publication.cljs` | Retain main's CMS store dependencies and write path, plus PR's wiki ownership dependency/check. |
| `frontend/src/pages/CmsPage.test.tsx` | Keep main's router line formatting and new navigation helper/tests. Conflicting PR line has identical props in another order. |
| `backend/src/cljs/knoxx/backend/infra/routes/auth.cljs` | Deliberately unresolved for the semantic blocker above. |

## Checks and limits

- Exactly one unresolved path remains (auth.cljs).
- Resolved JSON and YAML files parse successfully with Python json/PyYAML.
- `git diff --cached --check -- <resolved paths>` passes.
- Targeted clj-kondo of deps/shadow/app/publication/CMS files reports zero errors
  and one warning: `infra/routes/app/publication.cljs:76`, the combined registrar
  reaches 30 lines. This is visible and is not a zero-warning verification.
- Whole staged diff check reports 29 trailing blank-line findings inherited from
  source #305. No unrelated source cleanup was made during reconciliation.
- Backend typecheck, test/server builds, frontend suite, runtime/browser tests,
  and frozen dependency installation were not run: the auth merge deliberately
  remains unresolved, so this is not a buildable or verified integration tree.
- `mechanical-main-resolution.patch` contains only the mechanical decisions
  against origin/pr305, including the two destination files outside the
  original conflict list. It is a review aid, not a complete merge resolution.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Specify supported remote/embedded providers and preserve deliberate session/principal/membership semantics.
- [ ] Preserve main's deployment qualification and CMS revision history.
- [ ] Test remote and embedded sign-in, credential management, anonymous refusal, MCP authority and cross-host identity.
- [ ] Apply/reconcile layers without silently restoring retired deployment paths.
- [ ] Re-run backend/frontend gates and human acceptance against the actual reconciled head.

title: Project the eta-mu GitHub evidence graph and query contract
body:
## Objective

Use Knoxx as the indexed knowledge and graph surface behind the eta-mu GitHub bot. Ingest Axxium-bound GitHub observations and evidence records, build a replayable projection, and expose queries that let eta-mu and Sol retrieve exactly which artifacts support or contradict a review finding.

This extends the disabled interaction resources in `open-hax/knoxx#294`; it does not make Knoxx the webhook authority, event store, final review synthesizer, or installation-token owner.

## Minimum graph

### Nodes

- Axxium principal, provider account, GitHub App installation, actor, and execution episode
- repository, commit, tree, branch/ref, pull request, issue, review, review thread, review comment
- check suite, check run, annotation, workflow run, job, step
- test run, test case, build artifact, coverage report, log, trace
- contract/resource/rule and exact revision
- event-ledger stream, record, segment, manifest, checkpoint
- evidence worker, worker attempt, finding, synthesis decision, publication
- document, tag assertion, content identity, Drive mirror object

### Edges

`BOUND_TO`, `OBSERVED_AS`, `REVISION_OF`, `PARENT_OF`, `CHANGED_BY`, `CHECKED`, `PRODUCED`, `INSPECTED`, `SUPPORTS`, `CONTRADICTS`, `SUPERSEDES`, `REQUIRES`, `CAUSED_BY`, `MIRRORED_AS`, `PROJECTED_FROM`, `PUBLISHED_AS`, and `TAGGED_WITH`.

Every node and edge carries the source record IDs, stream positions, exact revisions, and projection version from which it was derived.

## Query contract

Support bounded, typed queries such as:

- What exact head was this conclusion bound to?
- Which required checks are missing, pending, skipped, stale, failed, or unavailable?
- Which unresolved review threads still apply to the current head?
- Which commits/files/contracts changed since the last clean review?
- Which test artifacts and logs support this finding, and are their hashes/revisions valid?
- Which worker inspected each artifact, with what rule revision and coverage?
- Which findings conflict, supersede older findings, or lack accessible evidence?
- Which `.ημ` ledgers and immutable Drive mirror objects contain the source records?
- Can the projection be deleted and rebuilt to the same logical identities and edges?

Queries must state coverage and truncation. Empty does not imply complete.

## Ingestion law

- Raw GitHub delivery records, hydrated object observations, test records, worker findings, and synthesis decisions remain distinct event profiles.
- Identity comes from Axxium bindings plus provider IDs; titles, paths, usernames, and hashes are not principal/object identity.
- Projection writes are idempotent by source record and projection revision.
- A later observation supersedes current projected state without deleting history.
- Projection failure cannot acknowledge or mutate source-ledger admission.
- Sensitive payload fields are redacted or excluded under declared policy while retaining verifiable hashes and coverage gaps.

## Bot-facing API

Expose a narrow CLJS/NBB-callable query boundary returning Clojure-shaped values, evidence record references, completeness status, and stable reason codes. Eta-mu consumes these queries for synthesis; Sol consumes them for worker artifact discovery. Neither receives a raw database client.

## Acceptance

- Contract/resource definitions for GitHub/evidence projection and queries remain disabled until adapters exist.
- Pure projection laws and replay tests cover duplicate records, out-of-order observations, stale heads, supersession, missing parents, conflicting findings, redaction, partial coverage, and deterministic rebuild.
- One integration fixture ingests a signed-delivery observation, check/test artifacts, parallel worker findings, and an eta-mu synthesis decision, then proves the queries above.
- Graph/query output cites source record IDs and exact revisions rather than unsupported summaries.

Related: `open-hax/foresight#69`, `open-hax/knoxx#294`, and eta-mu tracking issue “TRACKING: GitHub webhook to evidence-agent workflow”.

title: Operate Knoxx as the eta-mu GitHub context and review bot
body:
## Outcome

Run the eta-mu GitHub App through Knoxx's resource-native event, graph, search, and agent surfaces. Knoxx becomes the context-rich bot that can explain a repository object, retrieve prior evidence, and dispatch a bounded review workflow; it does not become the webhook signature authority, event ledger, identity provider, or final verdict publisher.

Related implementation and coordination:

- #294 — Axxium-bound GitHub source/driver/ledger/projection contracts;
- open-hax/eta-mu#323 — signed webhook admission and Knoxx/Sol dispatch;
- open-hax/eta-mu#324 — typed parallel evidence lanes;
- open-hax/foresight#69 — Axxium Event Fabric architecture;
- open-hax/katamorph#27 — portable GitHub interaction resources.

## System boundary

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  LEDGER[(admitted GitHub and evidence records)] --> PROJ[Knoxx projections]
  PROJ --> DOC[document index]
  PROJ --> GRAPH[knowledge graph]
  PROJ --> SEARCH[semantic and lexical search]

  EVENT[normalized GitHub event] --> ROUTE[Knoxx trigger and action runtime]
  ROUTE --> BOT[github_automation actor]
  DOC --> BOT
  GRAPH --> BOT
  SEARCH --> BOT
  BOT --> PLAN[typed review or response plan]
  PLAN --> ETA[eta-mu workflow coordinator]
  PLAN --> SOL[authorized Sol job]

  ETA --> RESULT[(evidence records)]
  SOL --> RESULT
  RESULT --> PROJ
```

## Bot experience

For a pull request, issue, review thread, check failure, or `@eta-mu` mention, the bot can answer from a bounded repository snapshot:

- what object triggered it and which exact revision is under review;
- which contracts, files, tests, ledgers, prior findings, and dependency revisions are relevant;
- what evidence exists, what is stale, and what remains unavailable;
- which workflow node is running or blocked;
- which agent owns the next bounded action;
- why a finding blocks, advises, or remains uncertain.

The bot should expose the same state through chat, GitHub Check details, and a Knoxx evidence view instead of generating three incompatible narratives.

## Required projection nodes

- GitHub installation, repository, commit, branch, pull request, issue, review, review thread, check suite/run, workflow run/job, file, comment, actor;
- Axxium principal, provider account, installation binding, object binding, stream, episode;
- ledger record, ledger segment, causal root/parent, test run, evidence artifact, finding, contradiction, verdict, publication receipt;
- Katamorph resource and revision, Proxx policy decision, Knoxx agent/run, Sol job/run.

Every projected node and edge retains the admitted record IDs and stream positions that produced it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Finish #294 with a registered driver, admissible source catalog, resolvable actor role/capability, and exact-head regression evidence.
- [ ] Add a runtime adapter that consumes only signature-verified, admitted GitHub events from eta-mu; Knoxx does not verify secrets from model context.
- [ ] Hydrate and project repository, pull request, issue, review, check, workflow, and file objects by immutable provider ID plus Axxium binding.
- [ ] Index `.ημ` and `.eta-mu` manifests/segments as discoverable objects without treating filenames or paths as identity.
- [ ] Project test/evidence records and their causal links so an agent can retrieve prior exact-head results without prompt stuffing.
- [ ] Add a `github_automation` agent contract using the canonical `github-event-observer` role and bounded event/graph/read tools.
- [ ] Add triggers for pull-request synchronization, review requests, review comments/mentions, check completion, and reconciliation findings.
- [ ] Route effects through eta-mu/Sol action contracts; the Knoxx agent emits a plan and evidence, not an ambient GitHub write.
- [ ] Add deterministic context packing with explicit byte/token limits, source identity, truncation/coverage records, and stable ordering.
- [ ] Add replay tests proving the same admitted history produces the same GitHub graph identities, trigger decisions, and context manifest.
- [ ] Add authorization tests proving an actor without the required Axxium installation/object grant cannot read or dispatch the object.
- [ ] Add an end-to-end fixture that asks the Knoxx bot about a seeded pull-request defect and returns the exact evidence record, changed line, and owning workflow node.
- [ ] Display partial, unavailable, stale, and contradictory evidence distinctly from absent evidence.

## First runtime slice

1. Accept one normalized `pull_request.synchronize` observation from eta-mu.
2. Project repository, commit, pull request, changed file, and `.ημ` locator nodes.
3. Trigger the `github_automation` actor.
4. Build a deterministic context manifest from graph, source, contracts, and prior evidence.
5. Emit a typed `review/requested` plan for eta-mu.
6. Admit the returned findings and project them back onto the pull request.
7. Prove replay equivalence.

## Non-goals

- No direct model access to GitHub App private keys or installation tokens.
- No graph-derived identity when Axxium/provider identity exists.
- No direct publication from an agent response.
- No second review ledger hidden inside Knoxx storage.
- No claim that the bot sees repositories, files, or comments outside its recorded installation coverage.

- [ ] Changed/new files, issues, and PRs after the checkpoint are returned exactly once; the checkpoint advances only after a successful scan.
- [ ] Incremental behavior works across multiple configured repositories without one repository's checkpoint affecting another.
- [ ] Tests exercise first scan, no-change rescan, changed-file rescan, changed issue/PR rescan, and failed-scan checkpoint preservation.
- [ ] Focused ingestion tests and lint pass on the exact head.

title: security: replace ingestion identity headers with scoped service delegation
body:
<!-- openhax-kanban-sync uuid="knoxx-ingestion-scoped-service-identity-handoff" -->

## Signal

The production translation worker in
`ingestion/src/kms_ingestion/translation/worker.clj` and the audio driver in
`ingestion/src/kms_ingestion/drivers/audio.clj` both call Knoxx with a configured API key and
`x-knoxx-user-email`; translation can also attach `x-knoxx-membership-id`. The configured
`KNOXX_USER_EMAIL` defaults to `system-admin@open-hax.local`, an ambient identity fallback.

The worker also has a live legacy single-job carrier: it polls `/translations/jobs/next`, starts
Knoxx work without batch membership, and calls `mark-job-status` for processing, complete, and
failed. That path needs explicit non-ambient job authority and cannot remain outside the sole-writer
transition model.

## Ownership and dependencies

Required child of #2. On protected routes, #2 must reject any public identity header combined with
session or API-key material before context or effect; there is no strip-and-continue outcome.

This issue owns the independently implementable JVM/service migration required before that rule can
ship without breaking translation or audio ingestion. It is coupled to #283's typed
translation-config authority, #275's attempt admission, and
`knoxx-translations-event-sourced` storage identity. PR #286 only plans and projects this work; it
does not deliver the delegation runtime. This issue remains an independent 8sp task.

## Authority and credential scope

- Remove every worker-emitted public identity header, the production `KNOXX_USER_EMAIL` input, and
  its fixed administrator default. Do not retain, rename, replace, or relocate that fallback.
- Give each deployment a machine credential that authenticates only a broker-only, membershipless
  ingestion service principal. Missing, malformed, expired, or unmapped credentials fail before a
  protected request. API key plus a public identity header is rejected, never stripped and
  continued.
- Audio may run as that service principal under explicit audio permissions. A raw ingestion API key
  can otherwise call only the named delegation broker; it cannot access the config repository or
  select a membership.
- For a batch, the broker verifies explicit delegation permission, one active membership, the
  organization, and current carrier data through the existing OpenPlanner adapter, then installs a
  Knoxx-owned source manifest and authority epoch. Only then it mints a sender-constrained
  `ProposalSelectionCapability` bound to the carrier tuple, source manifest, epoch, audience,
  expiry, and workload key, with exactly `source-manifest:read` and
  `translation-config:model-select`. After server validation of a `SegmentationProposal`, Knoxx
  installs a new immutable translation manifest containing the complete admitted coordinates. The
  legacy single-job path uses the same sequence with membership absent: job admission installs only
  a `SourceManifest` and epoch, then proposal selection/segmentation produces the
  `TranslationManifest` before any complete coordinate or bound job capability exists. Ambiguous,
  stale, cross-organization, or unowned work returns a typed non-effect.
- Mint a short-lived, audience-bound, sender-constrained capability as the sole delegated authority.
  It binds service principal, carrier type, batch/job id, membership when applicable, organization,
  manifest id/digest, authority epoch, operations, expiry, nonce, and workload signing-key
  thumbprint. Subsequent work uses capability plus possession proof, never API key plus capability
  or capability plus identity header.
- Under #283, the proposal-selection capability is the sole authority for one manifest-scoped model
  selection and returns no config payload. The later bound capability is distinct and may perform
  its manifest-scoped read-only config GET. Neither authorizes PATCH; ordinary membership-bearing
  API keys remain distinct member principals.
- Dynamic logical splitting is a two-phase path. Server-owned preflight uses the admitted
  `ProposalSelectionCapability` as sole repository authority to resolve and pin an immutable
  `ProposalModelSelection` containing the Knoxx config resource/version and catalog model
  id before the unbound `SegmentationProposal` run. The run receives that selected model and source
  manifest, but no config credential/payload, `save_translation`, config-admission,
  identity-minting, or candidate-persistence authority. Server validation exact-matches proposed
  spans to canonical bytes, derives complete coordinates and stable attempt/effect ids, and
  exact-matches config admission to the pinned selection; selection drift discards the proposal and
  restarts preflight. Only the separate bound run receives the immutable map of pre-admitted
  `AttemptEffectIdentity` values; `save_translation` exact-echoes one member and cannot mint identity.
- The event-owned production `save_translation` schema exposes the required stable `attempt_id` and
  required stable `effect_id`, selects the full pre-admitted `AttemptEffectIdentity`, and passes it
  unchanged through the save boundary. Its `CanonicalAttemptEvent` compares the full
  `AttemptEffectIdentity` plus delegated manifest id/digest and authority epoch, so no stable commit
  identity can disappear between the admitted map and OpenPlanner.

## Resource, request, and effect scope

- Define `SegmentCoordinate` as organization, project, garden, document, source language, source
  revision, authoritative source span/slice identity and digest, segment index, and target language.
  Event grouping and the current projection unique index use `SegmentCoordinate`.
  `AttemptIdentity = (SegmentCoordinate, stable attempt/event id)` supplies the event unique index,
  so different attempt ids on one coordinate remain intentional retranslations.
  `AttemptEffectIdentity = (AttemptIdentity, stable effect id)` supplies the exact-once ledger claim;
  the ledger never claims a segment coordinate globally. A delegated retry also exact-matches
  manifest id/digest and authority epoch as immutable facts. Substituting manifest, epoch, or effect
  identity conflicts with no new claim or write.
- A Knoxx-owned `DelegatedIngestionAuthorityStore` atomically validates the full
  `AttemptEffectIdentity`, manifest, epoch, and payload; appends the immutable attempt; claims the
  logical effect; and enqueues the existing `save-openplanner-segment!` adapter call. A local
  `ProjectionDispatchLease` serializes intents by the actual existing
  `LegacyProjectionKey = (org_id, document_id, segment_index, target_lang)`, binds that key to exactly
  one complete `SegmentCoordinate`, and permits at most one remote invocation per intent. A distinct
  project, garden, source language/revision, or source span that aliases the key returns
  `ProjectionKeyCollision` before a new claim or remote invocation. Because the existing OpenPlanner
  projection stores no causal
  attempt/effect token, an ambiguous response is never automatically redispatched: exact canonical
  read-back under the coordinate lease may install the receipt; otherwise an
  `AmbiguousProjectionOutcome` blocks completion and later same-coordinate projection dispatch for
  operator resolution without fabricating a receipt. OpenPlanner needs no new route, CAS primitive,
  epoch field, or atomicity guarantee.
- The proposal phase loads canonical source bytes from the admitted revision and exact-matches every
  proposed span/slice before the bound turn exists. Altered, ambiguous, gapped, overlapped,
  duplicated, reordered, or drifted content fails before config admission or candidate work.
  `save_translation` later selects only a pre-admitted member.
- Sign the method, canonical route, complete normalized request target/query, body digest,
  capability id/digest, timestamp, sequence, and proof id. Reject blank, duplicate, unknown, and
  ambiguous query encodings. Equivalent reordered queries canonicalize identically.
- Every validated selector is also consumed. `translation-segments-op` must exact-match and forward
  `document_id` plus every allowlisted selector to the adapter. Progress/terminal decisions use only
  receipts for the current manifest, epoch, and effect set/run—not generic segment counts or rows
  from another document/run/epoch.
- Delegated ingestion is OpenPlanner-segment-only. Its envelope cannot carry/select publication
  `dispatch_key`, publication `run_id`, or `save-publication-translation!`; injected publication
  discriminators fail before `content/write!`. The publication filesystem trigger/receipt protocol
  is outside this issue.

## One state owner

- A Knoxx-owned `DelegatedIngestionAuthorityStore` is the single manifest, epoch, effect-fence,
  transition-CAS, and outbox authority for delegated batch and legacy-job execution. Direct Mongo
  and REST modes wrap only the existing stable OpenPlanner client boundary.
- Migrate `next-batch!`, `update-batch!`, the update-status route, `mark-batch-status`,
  `mark-job-status`, arbitrary direct client setters, claim/attempt/progress writers, and mutable
  `resolve-dispatch!` terminal outcomes behind that Knoxx gateway.
- The local attempt/effect transaction and terminal transition share the Knoxx epoch. Outbox leases
  serialize adapter dispatch with terminal CAS: an effect is observed before terminal linearization
  or is never sent, and an old-epoch intent is refused locally.
- OpenPlanner carrier/segment fields are a derived projection reached through the existing adapter,
  not a competing epoch/terminal authority. Immutable translation and publication receipts remain
  evidence for their separate workflows.

## Acceptance

1. Exact RED/GREEN worker tests remove all ambient identity emission and prove any
   API-key/public-identity collision rejects before context/effect, while credentialless public
   reads remain non-authorizing.
2. Batch and legacy-job happy paths receive only their policy-admitted manifests/capabilities;
   arbitrary membership, tuple, manifest, epoch, sender, replay, route, or operation substitutions
   produce zero protected effects and no administrator fallback.
3. Source and coordinate negatives cover organization/project/garden/document/source
   language/revision/span/content/segment/target substitutions, including ambiguous/gapped/
   overlapped/reordered slices. The exact authoritative slice persists once. Two intentional
   retranslations with different stable attempt ids on the same `SegmentCoordinate` produce distinct
   events and consecutive ordinals while sharing one current projection; manifest/epoch/effect
   substitutions cannot mint another ledger claim.
4. At the Knoxx authority-store and existing OpenPlanner adapter boundary, two pre-admitted members
   on the same `SegmentCoordinate` with different stable attempt ids succeed once each and carry
   distinct full `AttemptEffectIdentity` values through admission, exact save echo, local commit,
   and outbox dispatch. Unknown or substituted facts produce no claim or dispatch; an equal retry
   returns its receipt. A lost response after projection application causes no second remote call or
   later same-coordinate overwrite: exact read-back reconciles under the lease, while a non-matching
   or unprovable outcome remains durably blocked without a claimed receipt. A separate complete
   coordinate with the same legacy four-field sink key is rejected before claim or dispatch.
5. Query proofs cover reordering/equivalence plus selector substitution, and an integration test
   proves every validated selector—including `document_id`—reaches the data query. Other-document
   and same-document/other-run/epoch rows cannot advance progress or completion.
6. Delegated envelopes can reach only `save-openplanner-segment!`; publication discriminators fail
   before any content write.
7. A writer inventory test fails if any batch/job claim, attempt, progress, completion, failure,
   revocation, or terminal outcome bypasses the Knoxx gateway. Completion/revocation and in-flight
   effect races prove one terminal receipt and zero post-transition dispatches while immutable
   evidence remains queryable. Both direct-Mongo and REST modes prove no new OpenPlanner protocol.
8. #283 tests preserve member-key behavior and keep the ingestion key broker-only. Before carrier
   admission there is zero config I/O; the proposal-selection capability can perform only one scoped
   model selection with no config payload, the distinct bound capability can perform only scoped
   read-only GET, and cross-use/general GET/PATCH or tuple/manifest/epoch/sender substitution fails
   before repository I/O.
9. Focused ingestion/backend suites, cross-process probes, compile/typecheck, full relevant suites,
   and strict changed-surface lint are green with exact-head evidence.

## Done when

Translation and audio ingestion use no public identity headers; batch and single-job work have one
sender-constrained, manifest-scoped authority; source bytes and the complete storage coordinate are
authoritative; every selector is consumed; delegated ingestion cannot reach publication content;
and every batch/job state mutation plus segment effect is serialized by the one Knoxx-owned
manifest/epoch CAS and outbox gateway over the existing OpenPlanner adapter. #2 can then enforce the
collision rule without losing worker behavior.

title: board: reconcile Knoxx issue projection state
body:
## Outcome

Reconcile Knoxx's live issue inbox to the card source of truth without deleting legitimate backlog or manufacturing new work.

- Adds canonical, live-tree-rebased cards for distinct open follow-ups #285, #258, and #2.
- Projects required child #287 for the ingestion-worker credential migration, records it as blocking #2, and keeps #2 at 8sp without claiming the JVM runtime is already delivered.
- Enriches and adopts the existing #246 publication-runtime epic.
- Keeps existing #175 as the canonical fail-closed route-guard owner; exact duplicate intake #9 was commented and closed as duplicate.
- Normalizes flat label frontmatter on five existing cards: PR #238 successors #273 (`knoxx-translation-config-publication-dependency-removal`), #275 (`knoxx-versioned-resolved-translation-config`), #282 (`knoxx-resource-repository-snapshot-observation`), #283 (`knoxx-translation-config-trusted-auth-context`), plus canonical route guard #175 (`knoxx-tenant-fail-closed-route-guard`).
- Records every decision and exact RED/GREEN evidence in Receipt River and Session Mycology.

## Live issue census

At successor head `bd56d568185ac37dfdbc9d30ce94c305b4be81a0`:

- 189 issues total
- 157 open
- 157 unique open canonical UUID markers
- 0 unmarked open issues
- 0 duplicate open UUID markers
- no issue other than demonstrated duplicate #9 was closed

The original five-item gap reduced to four distinct adoptions because #9 was semantically and UUID-identical to existing open #175.

## Successor repairs

1. Initial head `8311862` contradicted its #175 link with one “#9 owns” non-goal. Successor `c96ae91` repaired that ownership statement.
2. Exact-`c96ae91` Codex review found two stale implementation premises:
   - #258 now preserves the already-landed grant map, `TokenRecord` schema, and extern validation boundary, then scopes the remaining OAuth JSON round-trip and raw consumers.
   - #2 now covers both TypeScript and CLJS request helpers, the admin `Apply actor` storage UI, direct header-builder consumers, and generated assets. Its live scope is re-estimated from 2sp to 3sp.

Successor `aa03b297c3bb40c00941929b584146d489b742bb` addresses both findings. The focused contract was RED 0/12 on the exact `c96` tree-equivalent and GREEN 12/12 on `aa03`.
3. Exact-`aa03` Codex review found two further live-contract gaps:
   - #2 removed browser emitters but did not constrain the server branches that trust the same client identity headers before session/API-key resolution. The card now scopes `authz/resolve-request-context!`, `session/create-session-hook`, and `session/resolve-auth-context`, with direct-client and credential-precedence probes, and is re-estimated from 3sp to 5sp.
   - #258 incorrectly required schema-optional membership, organization, and actor fields to be present. The card now preserves their valid absence and rejects only malformed present values.

Successor `fd826371e4315d2334adc719e379c2bba8435787` addresses both exact-`aa03` findings. The focused contract was RED 0/9 on exact `aa03` and GREEN 9/9 on `fd82637`.
4. Exact-`fd82637` Codex review found the session/API-key collision remained ambiguous. The card now admits exactly one credential authority per request and rejects simultaneous session-cookie/API-key material before context resolution, without precedence or fallback, for same-principal, different-principal, and malformed combinations.

Successor `f88b8cf9971561081b7a4c1916b0eb3c8160e9e5` addresses that finding. The focused collision contract was RED 0/4 on the exact `fd82637` tree-equivalent and GREEN 4/4 on `f88b8cf`.
5. CodeRabbit's substantive pass found the existing open `TokenRecord` map accepts unknown keys, allowing a misspelled optional binding to disappear before email-based policy resolution. The card now tightens the one named schema/validator in place, rejects every unknown key before policy access, and explicitly preserves deliberate `membershipId` absence only through required email plus optional organization resolving one active membership.

Successor `9b67902403fa5c83a5a07b14d0c106bbd67af654` addresses that finding. The unknown-key contract was RED 0/5 on the exact `f88b8cf` tree-equivalent and GREEN 5/5 on `9b67902`.
6. Exact-`9b67902` Codex review found the closed key set omitted legitimate persisted `createdAt` / `expiresAt` token-data metadata. The card now declares that typed optional pair in the same named schema, requires both absent or a valid ordered ISO-8601 pair, preserves timestamp-free trusted/legacy core records under envelope TTL authority, retains the pair in token listing, and forbids it from authentication decisions.

Successor `df36237db42d71553dfbd982e2cec09bfb9ee4a8` addresses that finding. The token-metadata contract was RED 0/5 on the exact `9b67902` tree-equivalent and GREEN 5/5 on `df36237`.

7. Exact-`df36237` Codex review found client-selected identity could still cross Knoxx-owned service proxies: OpenPlanner combined forwarded identity with a server-held bearer credential, while ingestion cloned the full inbound header set. The card now inventories every credentialed service proxy, drops the whole inbound `x-knoxx-*` identity family before outbound construction, permits downstream identity only when rederived from verified server context through a named adapter, and covers direct read and mutation callers for both proxy families.

Successor `df051436d6286a6403ac0e38fe71f43fbc7e7790` addresses that finding. The service-proxy identity contract was RED 0/8 on the exact `df36237` tree-equivalent and GREEN 8/8 on `df05143`.

8. A real non-rate-limited CodeRabbit full review of exact `df05143` found the card's unconditional 401 rule contradicted its deliberately public proxy-read proof. The rule now applies only to protected or credential-required requests. Deliberately public reads remain compatible only without fabricated identity, privileged retry/fallback, or authority borrowed from a downstream server credential.

Successor `7a48e2060dc7f286dcd0681d0f37b7eca4a51132` addresses that finding. The public-read authentication contract was RED 0/4 on the exact `df05143` tree-equivalent and GREEN 4/4 on `7a48e20`.

9. Exact-`7a48e20` Codex review found the separately registered `GET /api/openplanner/v1/sessions` route bypasses the wildcard handler and calls `openplanner-client/sessions!` with Knoxx's server-held bearer credential. The card now names that dedicated credential-required route, requires verified Knoxx context before any downstream call, and proves unauthenticated/header-only callers cannot invoke the client or observe session/enrichment data.

Successor `c4560b25a4391d2411b11d70caafcb29b6bc9871` addresses that finding. The dedicated sessions-proxy contract was RED 0/4 on the exact `7a48e20` tree-equivalent and GREEN 4/4 on `c4560b2`.

10. The resulting full registration-table audit found six eta-mu/OpenCode admin list, status, and ingest routes in the same file. Status/ingest attach the fixed `system-kms-headers` identity and can reach or mutate KMS, while list routes expose local session data. The card now requires verified administrator permission before every local observation or downstream effect and treats fixed KMS identity only as an operation-scoped service credential constructed after authorization.

Successor `fadf41fff35e31fb5274bd474104429049434b79` records that proactive closure. The admin KMS-boundary contract was RED 0/6 on the exact `c4560b2` tree-equivalent and GREEN 6/6 on `fadf41f`.

11. Exact-`fadf41f` Codex review found that slugless OAuth consent is legitimate but `authorization-code-payload` materializes `:orgSlug ""` and `persist-access-token!` copies it, so the planned closed token schema would reject a newly issued valid token. The token card now requires both OAuth writers to preserve optional absence through a slugless consent-to-token round trip. A full internal identity-emitter audit also found `infra.clients.knoxx-control/headers-for` combines a fixed administrator header with its API key, while agent-turn media serializes verified context back into indistinguishable public identity headers for loopback fetches. The identity card now requires one API-key authority for protected self-control calls and a named context-bound internal media adapter, and is re-estimated from 5sp to 8sp.

Successor `c743200c2e4d419283fb58db6e267671882bed18` addresses the exact finding and proactive compatibility audit. Against the exact `fadf41f` tree-equivalent, the slugless OAuth contract was RED 0/5 and the internal identity-handoff contract was RED 0/8; both are GREEN 5/5 and 8/8 on `c743200`.

12. Exact-`c743200` Codex review completed the identity-emitter inventory and found two production JVM callers outside the backend tree. `ingestion/src/kms_ingestion/translation/worker.clj` sends the API key with user email and optional batch membership; `ingestion/src/kms_ingestion/drivers/audio.clj` sends the API key with user email; and configuration supplies an ambient `system-admin@open-hax.local` default. Immediate collision rejection would break both workers, while simply dropping the batch header would erase legitimate per-batch membership semantics.

Successor `6ba6bdd955fa8a9d1b0788c1593eefb4b585e5ef` projects new issue/card #287 as the required independently estimated child of 8sp issue #2. The child makes the API key authenticate only a server-mapped ingestion service principal, keeps audio service-only, and represents batch membership as a policy-admitted short-lived capability bound to the service principal, batch, membership, organization, operations, audience, expiry, and nonce. Arbitrary selection, tuple swaps, expiry, replay, forgery, cross-route reuse, and credential combinations must produce zero protected effects. PR #286 records this dependency and proof contract only; it does not claim the broader JVM delegation runtime is delivered. The focused contract was RED 0/10 on the exact `c743200` tree-equivalent and GREEN 10/10 on `6ba6bdd`.

13. A real non-rate-limited CodeRabbit full review of exact `6ba6bdd` completed with no actionable issues. Fresh exact-head Codex then found two asynchronous lifecycle gaps in #287. First, capability rejection after `/api/knoxx/direct/start` did not bind or recheck the admitted tuple inside the spawned agent's later `save_translation` effects, so completion/revocation could race with protected writes. Second, a reusable nonce-bearing capability with a multi-call budget could not distinguish legitimate polling from an exact same-route replay.

Successor `dc9588a65631d4209c08fd2733930f6d47b728e8` addresses both findings. A spawned run now owns an immutable server authority envelope and authorization lease; the named `save_translation` boundary rechecks the tuple and a commit fence, while completion/revocation atomically closes the lease, invalidates fences, and cancels work so zero post-transition writes occur. Delegated calls use a capability sender-constrained to the workload signing key plus a fresh request proof as one credential authority. Proof identity is atomically consumed and exact/concurrent replays return a cached receipt or typed non-effect without duplicating work. Against the exact `6ba6bdd` tree-equivalent the focused lifecycle contract was RED 0/7; it is GREEN 7/7 on `dc9588a`, with the retained ingestion contract GREEN 10/10.

14. Exact-`dc9588a` review and a complete live-source authority inventory found that the delegated-ingestion plan still lacked a complete immutable resource identity, canonical-query consumption, one terminal writer/epoch owner, non-ambient legacy-job authority, authoritative source-slice binding, a safe publication-sink boundary, and consistent sibling contracts for API-key types and collision rejection. The consolidated repair now:
   - distinguishes membership-bearing member API keys from the broker-only ingestion service principal, rejects public identity-header collisions before context/effects, and admits membershipless legacy jobs only through explicit service permission plus organization, manifest, and epoch;
   - defines one complete `SegmentCoordinate` across #287, #275, and the event projection; separates it from stable `AttemptIdentity` and `AttemptEffectIdentity`; and propagates the full pre-admitted attempt/effect identity, manifest, epoch, source span/slice, and canonical payload through `save_translation` to the atomic writer;
   - signs and consumes the complete normalized request target including every query selector, scopes progress to the current manifest/epoch/effect set, and rejects cross-document/run/epoch substitutions;
   - narrows delegated ingestion to the OpenPlanner segment sink before content I/O and places every batch/job/status writer behind one OpenPlanner-owned manifest+epoch CAS gateway, preserving immutable evidence without a second terminal truth.

The semantic cross-card fixture was RED 13/19 on the exact predecessor and GREEN 19/19 on the repaired five-card candidate. All 17 retained executable contracts pass 137/137. Successive independent audits exposed and drove repairs for event/projection uniqueness, membershipless legacy jobs, end-to-end attempt/effect propagation, repeated same-coordinate turn members, and the production save/event schema. The final semantic diff `eb019b61616a4ef504c1838389e35dd93e5fd6589125956c9884406354dac177` (patch-id `e8cf15e2aa4ec21faa3c6308360a988c0ea69648`) received an independent exact-binding verdict of CLEAN: 0 P1 / 0 P2 / 0 P3.

15. Exact successor `91e1174e5b6562aa2184d3113609c8320832c9d1` preserves the five audited card blobs byte-for-byte and adds only the mechanically bound Session Mycology and Receipt River provenance. A second independent append-only audit verified the seven-file tree, full diff SHA-256 `6e1d9f29e211d074f904463045aaf48ff55a52ec1c568fcf2e6be8d8a6eccb8b`, stable patch-id `7f42a1fe911b22dc1bf0d415673627a120175048`, all EDN/Markdown/Rheos/integrity gates, and returned CLEAN: 0 P1 / 0 P2 / 0 P3. Live issue bodies #2, #275, #283, and #287 now exactly match their audited drafts and remain open; #2 and #287 remain distinct 8sp parent/child backlog items. PR #286 remains planning/projection only and does not claim the JVM delegation runtime or publication filesystem transaction has shipped.

16. Exact-`91e1174` review left four coupled contract failures. Successor
`bd56d568185ac37dfdbc9d30ce94c305b4be81a0` closes them without production or
cross-repository implementation:
   - turn admission now rejects a repeated `AttemptIdentity` even when `effect_id` differs, so
     config admission cannot accept a member the event unique index must reject;
   - migration persists and uniquely indexes a coordinate-independent `LegacyMigrationIdentity`
     from stable legacy storage identity, then compares coordinate/payload drift through that slot;
   - the live model-selected split behavior becomes an unbound `SegmentationProposal` phase with
     no save/config/candidate authority, followed by validation, atomic admission, and a separate
     bound translation turn; and
   - manifest/epoch CAS, effect fences, terminal transitions, and the outbox remain in a Knoxx-owned
     `DelegatedIngestionAuthorityStore` over the existing OpenPlanner adapter.

The focused successor harness (SHA-256
`79f220cf189049884ca6385f0d0d1e9378a66b752de435391dfcf5b9c8ae1734`) is RED
0/12 on detached exact predecessor `91e1174` and GREEN 12/12 on the successor.
Rheos remains 261 tasks / 14 columns with no drift; Markdown reports zero issues, Receipt River
parses 280 forms, and `git diff --check` is clean. Live issue projections #275 and #287 were
updated to the same corrected laws.

17. Fresh exact-`bd56d568` review found two successor contract gaps. Exact successor
`a552c4b74cef6c369de3947c48964e6d67e32a33` closes both without changing production code or the existing OpenPlanner protocol:
   - server-owned preflight now resolves and pins `ProposalModelSelection` from Knoxx config
     authority before the unbound segmentation turn; later config admission must exact-match that
     config version/model or discard the proposal and restart; and
   - a Knoxx-owned `ProjectionDispatchLease` serializes each complete coordinate and permits at
     most one existing-sink invocation per intent. A lost response is reconciled only by exact
     canonical read-back under the lease; otherwise `AmbiguousProjectionOutcome` blocks completion
     and later same-coordinate projection dispatch with no redispatch or fabricated receipt.

The extended harness (SHA-256
`260ab06227acd992746c2744a1eff4bf3060ae20d811add37010e8f8015e4db0`) is RED
12/16 on exact predecessor `bd56d568` and GREEN 16/16 on this successor. Issue #287 carries the
same proposal-model and ambiguous-projection laws.

18. Fresh exact-`a552c4b7` review found that server ownership alone did not authorize proposal
config preflight. Exact successor `e2e62c6aee006631b22d2837a22a563ecd39be1d` defines a typed, sender-constrained
`ProposalSelectionCapability` only after verified carrier and `SourceManifest` admission. Its
closed operations are `source-manifest:read` plus one `translation-config:model-select`; it
exposes neither config payload nor reusable GET/PATCH authority. The later bound capability remains
distinct, and #283/#287 plus the event/config cards now share this law.

The extended harness (SHA-256
`68381cb67288d9b2f3e9253934119b7f17a413e9baafbba00c2df346e709ed3c`) is RED
16/18 on exact predecessor `a552c4b7` and GREEN 18/18 on this successor.

19. Fresh exact-`e2e62c6a` review found two remaining ordering/key mismatches. Exact successor
`edbdce312ea165f179992b7ce2710e505fd5fc2b` makes membershipless legacy jobs follow the same
`SourceManifest` → `SegmentationProposal` → `TranslationManifest` sequence as batches, and
moves `ProjectionDispatchLease` to the actual existing OpenPlanner
`LegacyProjectionKey = (org_id, document_id, segment_index, target_lang)`. The reservation binds
one complete coordinate; any distinct complete coordinate that aliases that legacy key returns
`ProjectionKeyCollision` before claim or dispatch.

The extended harness (SHA-256
`b0008542e030039435bf738cc98b95029f96896026d1672393ccc3ef223f03b3`) is RED
18/20 on exact predecessor `e2e62c6a` and GREEN 20/20 on this successor.

20. A fresh exact-`edbdce31` Codex pass found two broader omissions after CodeRabbit's clean review
of that head. Exact successor `0b637f7dab5b37ba92f3b13394a4bbd2e7b004d0` adds the active
`/api/data/op/*`, `/api/data/mongo/{list,query}`, and
`/api/data/jobs/build-semantic-edges` handlers to the fail-closed bearer-proxy inventory, and
defines migration-only `LegacyUnknownSourceCoordinate` for rows whose historical revision/span
cannot be proven. Unknown provenance stays servable without being attributed to current source and
cannot authorize provenance-sensitive use or a new append.

The extended harness (SHA-256
`9612c13fb951e3049eab14816e04690c972996f79cfc0c32883b645f39d59f69`) is RED
20/22 on exact predecessor `edbdce31` and GREEN 22/22 on this successor. Issues #2 and #275 carry
the same laws.

21. CodeRabbit's non-rate-limited pass posted three actionable predecessor findings after successor
work had begun. Exact successor `a6fab4525c0fd531540a0870a65c47f0cca257a5` requires concrete fixture ids, valid bodies, expected
statuses, and validating stubs for publication live probes; proves credential and response scope for
every deliberately public read; and makes config GET reject all public-identity/session-or-key
collisions before context/repository observation.

The extended harness (SHA-256
`08db5e24bdcc0be362c5c2c274da75684ef75f1c284ee2c4b2f744fbd08f1fff`) is RED
22/25 on the semantic predecessor and GREEN 25/25 on this successor. Issues #246, #2, and #275 carry
the same laws.

22. Fresh Codex review found the separately registered bearer-backed
`GET /api/data/mongo/collections` dashboard route was absent from the active data-proxy inventory.
Exact successor `c2480c06c59130a936e0f415fbb08663c8bd3b30` adds it to both the concrete inventory
and direct no-context/identity-header-only probe matrix before `documents-stats!` or
`graph-monitoring!` may make a downstream call.

The extended harness (SHA-256
`4dc94eb5f6fc444d91889b858258590c94f372c367e5a3a2213e1599fad3af2b`) is RED
24/25 on exact predecessor `a6fab452` and GREEN 25/25 on this successor.

title: Bind translation-config scope to trusted authentication context
body:
<!-- openhax-kanban-sync uuid="knoxx-translation-config-trusted-auth-context" -->

## Signal

`GET /api/translations/config` currently reaches `authz/resolve-request-context!`, whose
header-first path accepts client-supplied identity and organization hints. A caller can select
another active membership before the route resolves its `EffectiveConfigView`.

Evidence: [PR #238 review](https://github.com/open-hax/knoxx/pull/238#discussion_r3887454201) at exact head
`8c22440a0fe91f16f5a7ef203ee370f150733f58`.

## Typed authority contract

- Ordinary membership-bearing API keys and verified sessions derive their configured member
  principal, membership, roles, and organization. On protected config routes, adding any public
  identity header rejects the request before context/repository I/O; there is no
  strip-and-continue case.
- #287's ingestion API key is a separate broker-only, membershipless service-principal credential.
  The raw key can call only the delegation broker; it cannot select membership, access the config
  repository, perform translation-config GET, or perform PATCH.
- For a batch, the broker verifies active membership, explicit delegation permission, matching
  organization, current batch manifest, and authority epoch. For a legacy job, membership is absent;
  the broker verifies service-principal job permission, matching organization, current job manifest,
  and authority epoch. A membership-bearing job fails as the wrong carrier type. After carrier and
  `SourceManifest` admission, a sender-constrained `ProposalSelectionCapability` binds that tuple,
  manifest, epoch, audience, expiry, and workload key. Its only config operation is one
  `translation-config:model-select` observation; preflight exposes the immutable config version and
  catalog model id, never config payload or reusable GET authority. After translation-manifest
  admission, the distinct bound capability may GET only its manifest-scoped organization, project,
  garden, source/target-language view. Neither capability can PATCH; API key plus capability and
  cross-use of one capability for the other's operation are collisions.
- Missing, expired, forged, revoked, or unconfigured authority fails before permission checks,
  repository access, mutation, or value/existence disclosure.
- Preserve existing member read permissions, platform-only global mutation policy, config
  precedence, response shape, and the single facade/resolver.

## Proof / acceptance

1. Organization-A member credentials cannot be redirected to B by public identity headers; every
   collision rejects before repository I/O. Header-only protected requests remain unauthenticated.
2. Ordinary membership-bearing API keys retain their admitted no-header GET/PATCH behavior.
3. A raw #287 ingestion key reaches only the broker and performs zero config repository I/O. Before
   carrier and `SourceManifest` admission, no proposal-selection authority exists.
4. A valid `ProposalSelectionCapability` requires the verified carrier tuple, source manifest,
   epoch, audience, expiry, and workload key and may perform exactly one model-selection observation
   returning no config payload. Swap/replay any fact, request general GET/PATCH, or use it after
   selection drift and prove failure before I/O or disclosure. A valid bound batch capability
   requires active membership, delegation permission, organization, translation manifest, and epoch.
5. A valid legacy-job capability requires membership absent plus service-principal job permission,
   organization, current job manifest, and epoch. Adding membership or swapping another fact fails
   before I/O. Each carrier as sole authority can GET exactly its manifest-scoped view;
   API-key-plus-capability fails too.
6. Capability-authorized PATCH always fails before mutation, while ordinary platform PATCH remains
   compatible and organization administrators remain denied.
7. Unit/route integration tests, real-server E2E, backend compile, coverage, and the complete auth
   suite pass.

## Relationships

- Blocks the trusted-scope acceptance of #275.
- Coupled to #287: membership-bearing API keys remain member principals; the ingestion credential
  is broker-only and gains only capability-derived read scope after admission.
- Complements `knoxx-tenant-fail-closed-route-guard`; this issue prevents caller bytes from
  manufacturing a non-nil context.

title: Add provider-neutral multi-resource snapshot observations
body:
<!-- openhax-kanban-sync uuid="knoxx-resource-repository-snapshot-observation" -->

## Signal

PR #238 exact-head review found that immutable resolved translation config requires one consistent observation of the global config and optional organization override, but the repository contract currently exposes only single-resource resolve/list/write operations. Sequential reads can mint provenance for a combination that never existed, and a caller-supplied absence marker cannot prove an override was absent.

Evidence: https://github.com/open-hax/knoxx/pull/238#discussion_r3887406555 at head `6f5b6bc07bbd5420f6170d536b7cfd4ec85ebfcc`.

## Scope

- Extend the existing provider-neutral resource repository boundary with one multi-resource observation operation over an ordered canonical identity set and authenticated actor context.
- Linearize the requested reads at one repository state and return one immutable observation identity plus a present entry (canonical record and resource-scoped version) or repository-authoritative absence entry for every requested identity.
- Authorize every requested identity before existence/version disclosure, preserving non-enumerating denial.
- Keep observation identity scoped to the requested identities/results so unrelated writes do not rotate it; a requested resource update or absent-to-present transition changes the next observation.
- Implement the same semantics for the fake and file/EDN providers. A future remote provider must satisfy the same compatibility suite without exposing provider mechanics.
- Use the existing repository authority; do not add a translation-only read path, shadow store, or second precedence implementation.

## Proof / acceptance

- A forced update between the two would-be single reads returns either one complete before-state or one complete after-state, never a torn combination.
- An override create racing an observation returns either authoritative absence or the new present revision at the operation's linearization point.
- Unrelated writes preserve the observation identity and selected resource versions.
- Cross-tenant existing and missing identities are indistinguishable and disclose no partial observation.
- Fake and file providers pass the identical operation/shape/error/concurrency suite; file tests are cross-process, not only in-memory.
- The result supplies the snapshot/absence prerequisite consumed by #275.

## Relationships

- Consumer: #275.
- Repository prerequisite: `knoxx-file-resource-repository-provider` under `knoxx-resource-repository-cms`.
- Distinct from #273, which removes publication dependencies from the existing config facade.

## Signal

`knoxx.backend.infra.routes.translation-config/resolved-config!` currently returns only effective
configuration values. The translation pipeline requires immutable provenance, but contributing
resource revisions disappear after resolution.

Evidence: PR #238 exact-head review at `70e1dc13960aee63e8138ac03b9a3fb0708e9ce9`, review
comment 3887319406.

## Scope

- Evolve the existing `resolved-config!` boundary; do not add a parallel configuration authority.
- Preserve exact contributing configuration/catalog/policy revisions, repository observation and
  authorization receipts, effective organization/delegation, schema/policy version, and a
  deterministic attested artifact identity through provider invocation and durable evidence.
- Use #283's typed trusted authority: membership-bearing session/API-key scope or, for #287, an
  admitted sender-constrained capability as the sole authority for manifest-scoped read-only GET.
  The raw broker-only ingestion key cannot inspect config and a capability never authorizes PATCH.
- Use the same complete immutable segment coordinate as
  `knoxx-translations-event-sourced` and #287 for `AttemptIdentity`: organization, project, garden,
  document, source language, source revision, authoritative source span/slice identity and digest,
  segment index, and target language, plus caller-stable `attempt_id`.
- Every admitted turn member adds a stable effect id to its `AttemptIdentity`, forming its
  `AttemptEffectIdentity`. A #287 delegated attempt additionally binds carrier type and manifest id/digest,
  plus Knoxx-owned authority epoch. Substituting manifest, epoch, or effect identity
  conflicts before config observation, ledger claim, provider invocation, or save.
- A dynamic-split path first runs an unbound `SegmentationProposal` session over manifest-bound
  canonical source bytes. It cannot call `save_translation`, observe/admit config, mint identity,
  or persist a candidate. Server validation derives the complete coordinates and stable ids before
  launching a separate bound translation turn.
- The atomic turn admission pre-admits each member's full `AttemptEffectIdentity` and carries its
  canonical map through authenticated server context; `save_translation` only exact-echoes a
  selected stable attempt/effect pair and cannot create either identity after provider work.
- The ordered member map is keyed by complete `AttemptEffectIdentity`, with a second uniqueness
  check on embedded `AttemptIdentity`. Members may share `SegmentCoordinate` only when their
  stable attempt ids make `AttemptIdentity` distinct. A repeated `AttemptIdentity` with a
  different effect id is rejected before persistence; the repeated coordinate alone is valid.
- Preserve publication-free namespace closure from #273 and the existing one-facade inspection/
  attempt-admission law.

## TDD / evidence

1. Global-only and organization-override resolution preserve exact ordered revisions,
   authorization evidence, absence witnesses, and stable artifact identity.
2. Config/catalog/policy rotation admits one coherent observation and never rewrites an already
   admitted attempt's provenance.
3. Cross-tenant, client-fabricated, stale, missing, receipt-replayed, or value/revision-mismatched
   artifacts fail before provider invocation without an existence leak.
4. Reuse one raw `attempt_id` across coordinates differing only by project, garden, document,
   source language/revision/span, segment index, or target language; each is independently admitted.
   Changed reuse within one complete coordinate conflicts consistently at config and event gates.
5. Two distinct `AttemptIdentity` values on one coordinate coexist in the same atomic turn map as
   intentional retranslations: the event unique index uses `AttemptIdentity`, the member map uses
   full `AttemptEffectIdentity`, and the current projection unique index uses the complete coordinate.
   A duplicate full member identity and the same `AttemptIdentity` paired with another effect id
   are rejected without rejecting a coordinate shared by distinct attempts. A delegated retry with
   a substituted manifest, epoch, or effect id conflicts before observation, provider work, or
   another ledger claim.
6. #283 member credentials retain compatible behavior; the raw ingestion key performs no repository
   I/O; admitted capability GET is narrowly scoped; delegated PATCH fails before mutation.
7. Existing adapter/consumer compile, focused/full tests, real-boundary E2E, and publication-free
   closure are green.

## Dependencies

- #273 for publication-free law/domain/loader closure.
- #282 and the provider-neutral repository contracts for exact multi-resource observations.
- #283 for typed trusted config scope.
- #287 and `knoxx-translations-event-sourced` for the shared complete immutable attempt identity.

## Done when

The production boundary yields one authenticated, immutable, versioned artifact whose exact
configuration provenance and complete attempt coordinate survive provider selection and durable
transduction evidence. Delegated attempts also retain manifest/Knoxx-epoch identity, and neither the
legacy short grouping key nor a new manifest can alias an installed attempt.


## PR #286 legacy unknown-provenance migration

A legacy row whose persisted `source_text` cannot be proven against one historical revision/span migrates under a tagged `LegacyUnknownSourceCoordinate` bound to its `LegacyMigrationIdentity`, persisted source-text digest, recorded locale/project/garden facts, and `:historical-source-unavailable`. Migration never attributes it to the current revision or fabricates a span. The record remains servable after cutover but is ineligible for provenance-sensitive evaluation, training, publication, or a new append; a later verified retranslation uses a separate normal `SegmentCoordinate`.


## PR #286 config-read collision law

`GET /api/translations/config` rejects any public `x-knoxx-*` identity header combined with session or API-key material using the canonical credential-collision failure before context resolution or repository observation, including a header value matching the authenticated organization/principal. It never ignores the header and continues.

title: refactor(mcp): make the token record a CLJS map across its producers and consumers
body:
<!-- openhax-kanban-sync uuid="knoxx-mcp-token-record-cljs-map" -->

Follow-up from #256, where the scope was agreed to be too large for that PR.

## The violation

`infra.auth.method-config/grant->token-record` returns a JavaScript object via `clj->js`, from an `infra.*` namespace. AGENTS.md is explicit:

> `knoxx.backend.extern.*` is the only place raw JavaScript interop should be born, decoded, encoded, sequenced, or mutated. Domain, law, shape, and ordinary infra code should receive and return CLJS maps/vectors/scalars.

## Why it was not fixed in #256

A token record has **two producers** feeding one consumer:

- `infra.auth.method-config/grant->token-record` — the authentication-contract path
- `infra.routes.mcp/load-token-record!` — the OAuth store path

`resolve-post-token-record!` returns one or the other, and everything downstream consumes the result as a JavaScript object:

- `resolve-token-context!` — `aget` for `membershipId`, `userEmail`, `orgSlug`
- the actor-scoping path — `aget` for `actorId`
- the tool-granting path — `array-seq` over `tools`, with a `^js` hint on the parameter

Converting one producer alone leaves the two branches disagreeing in type, which is strictly worse than the violation. Converting the type properly means changing every consumer in that route — pre-existing code that predates #256, and the part of the MCP surface with the thinnest test coverage.

## What the work is

1. Make both producers return a CLJS map with keyword keys.
2. Convert `resolve-token-context!`, the actor-scoping path and the tool-granting path to read that map.
3. Push the `clj->js` conversion down to the extern adapter that owns the MCP transport, if the transport still needs a JS object at all.
4. Drop the `^js` hints that become wrong.

## Why it is worth doing

The `aget`-on-token-record pattern is what made the auth-contract path easy to get wrong in the first place: a field name typo in either producer is silent, because `aget` on a missing key is `nil` rather than an error. A keyword-keyed map with a schema at the boundary makes both producers checkable against the same shape.

Ideally paired with a Malli shape for the record, so the two producers are validated against one contract rather than agreeing by convention.
